question: Regulation (EU) 2024/900 on the transparency and targeting of political advertising (TTPA) has understandably been met with considerable discontent at regional and local level. This is due to the extensive transparency obligations: all political advertising must clearly disclose who commissioned and financed it, its intended purpose, who created it and which audiences it seeks to target.
For volunteer-based structures in regions and municipalities in particular, this represents a disproportionate amount of red tape and raises serious concerns about possible high fines. 1.

Does the Commission plan to evaluate the TTPA, in particular with regard to its impact at regional and local level, and to put forward a proposal to resolve the bureaucratic hurdles that have arisen in practice?
Is it considering limiting the scope of the regulation to online political advertising and excluding the regional and local levels from it?
